inputs.text: This is being sold as a transparency push, but it looks more like outside institutions helping shape the Dominican Republic’s rules—and calling that “integrity.” On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader watching. The polished anti-corruption language is useful cover: whoever gets to define the standards also gets influence over how the country is governed.

output.main_topic: Agreement to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy

central_relations.subject: Roberto Álvarez
central_relations.action: signed an agreement with Mathias Cormann in Paris to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy
central_relations.base_action: signed an agreement to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy

central_relations.subject: Luis Abinader
central_relations.action: watched Roberto Álvarez and Mathias Cormann sign the agreement

output.narrative_frame: The agreement is framed skeptically as a possible channel for outside influence over the Dominican Republic’s governance, despite its anti-corruption and transparency language.
opinions: The agreement is framed as a transparency push but may help outside institutions shape the Dominican Republic’s rules.
Anti-corruption language is presented as useful cover, while those who define standards gain influence over governance.
